mfg1-electrical-l050.title: Design, manufacturing, logistics quality, and 4M
mfg1-electrical-l050.objective: Distinguish quality stages and investigate 4M changes through facts.

paragraphs.title: Start with customer requirements
paragraphs.text: Quality concerns how well performance, safety, reliability, and other customer requirements are met, not just the manufacturer’s convenience. Design quality is the intended characteristics; manufacturing quality is how well they are realized; logistics quality concerns items, quantities, timing, and condition until delivery.

paragraphs.title: QCD and safety
paragraphs.text: Q means quality, C cost, and D delivery. Even when considering safetyS alongside them, do not remove safety devices to meet deadlines. Reworking defects affects time and trust as well as material cost.

paragraphs.title: Use 4Mto examine changes
paragraphs.text: Man means workers, Machine equipment, Material materials, and Method procedures. Do not blame people alone for increased defects: compare material lots, tool condition, changed settings, and training. If several things changed together, record their respective times and scopes.

terms.meaning: Quality targeted and specified in design.
The quality actually achieved through manufacturing.
The combined viewpoints of quality, cost, and delivery.
The viewpoints of people, machines, materials, and methods.

mfg1-electrical-l050.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
List 4Mfactors when crimp defects increase just before a deadline. Propose holding and reporting while preserving customer requirements and safety.
safety: Do not omit safety or inspection requirements because of deadlines or cost.
mfg1-electrical-l050.summary: Distinguish quality stages and investigate 4M changes through facts.

mfg1-electrical-l051.title: Verify causes with the three actuals and PDCA
mfg1-electrical-l051.objective: Verify facts under comparable conditions, and connect evaluation to the next plan.

paragraphs.title: Actual place, item, and facts
paragraphs.text: The three actuals emphasize where the issue occurs, the item involved, and verified facts. Do not settle a cause from reports alone; examine the location and item within approved safe boundaries. This does not mean touching a dangerous object directly.

paragraphs.title: Connect planning with evaluation
paragraphs.text: Plan sets the target and method, Do implements them, Check compares results against the target, and Act feeds findings into the next cycle. A single implementation does not guarantee effectiveness; align comparison periods, quantities, and other conditions.

paragraphs.title: Describe change numerically
paragraphs.text: Under the same inspection method,6 defects in 200 becoming 2 in 200 means a rate reduction from 3%to 1%. If materials or production conditions also changed, however, the measure alone is not yet proven to be the cause. Report facts, inferences, and further checks separately.

terms.meaning: Understanding facts through the actual place, actual item, and actual situation.
The cycle of planning, implementation, evaluation, and improvement.
A point at which a condition became different from before.
The proportion of defects within the inspected quantity.

mfg1-electrical-l051.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
For an improvement from 3%to 1%, write four columns: target, implementation record, comparison conditions, and next review. Add safe conditions for examining the actual item.
safety: Follow isolation, entry conditions, and assigned responsibilities when examining an actual item.
mfg1-electrical-l051.summary: Verify facts under comparable conditions, and connect evaluation to the next plan.

mfg1-electrical-l052.title: Compare work standards with QC process charts
mfg1-electrical-l052.objective: Check instructions and control conditions separately, including abnormal responses.

paragraphs.title: Reproduce the same work
paragraphs.text: Work standards specify sequence, method, equipment, tools, and key points. Check the latest revision, applicable part number, and machine. Do not overwrite standards with your own improvement: obtain approval and communicate the change before applying it.

paragraphs.title: What, when, and how to control
paragraphs.text: A QC process chart states the process, controlled characteristics, methods, frequency, responsibility, and abnormal responses. Check not only “caliper” but also measurement position, specification, sampling conditions, and record destination. The chart and work standard have different purposes and complement each other.

paragraphs.title: Do not independently change frequency
paragraphs.text: Once per lot is not the same as once per hour. Checks may also be required for first pieces, tool changes, or changed settings. Identify and hold defects and investigate the affected scope, including when results were last normal.

terms.reading: さぎょうひょうじゅん
terms.meaning: A standard defining work content, sequence, and methods.

terms.reading: きゅーしーこうていず
terms.meaning: A chart showing what each process controls, how, and how often.
A product first checked after production starts or changes.
Updating the contents of a document or similar item.

mfg1-electrical-l052.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
For terminal tightening, separately write key work-instruction points and QC characteristics, frequency, and abnormal responses. Write a request for clarification when revisions differ.
safety: Do not start work by guessing from an old or inapplicable standard.
mfg1-electrical-l052.summary: Check instructions and control conditions separately, including abnormal responses.

mfg1-electrical-l053.title: Separate counts, relationships, and possible causes with QC tools
mfg1-electrical-l053.objective: Choose tools for their purpose, and distinguish a diagram’s appearance from proof of cause.

paragraphs.title: Define before collecting
paragraphs.text: A check sheet specifies items, period, target, and counting rules. Choose bar, line, or pie graphs to match the purpose. When totals or denominators differ, comparing counts alone can mislead; check proportions too.

paragraphs.title: Distribution is different from relationship
paragraphs.text: Histograms show distributions, control charts show a process over time, and scatterplots show relationships between two variables. Correlation in a scatterplot does not prove one variable causes the other. Check conditions and outliers.

paragraphs.title: Distinguish candidates from evidence
paragraphs.text: A cause-and-effect diagram organizes possible causes using 4Mor similar categories. A Pareto chart helps select high-count categories, but do not ignore rare severe safety events. Verify proposed causes through measurements and comparisons rather than assigning blame without evidence.

terms.meaning: A table that gathers data using defined items.
A plot displaying paired values of two variables as points.
A diagram linking a problem to organized possible causes.
A relationship observed between two quantities.

mfg1-electrical-l053.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Plan an investigation of a temperature-versus-dimension scatterplot. Describe what to record, correlation versus causation, and possible causes to place in a cause-and-effect diagram.
safety: Do not falsely record a possible cause as a confirmed cause.
mfg1-electrical-l053.summary: Choose tools for their purpose, and distinguish a diagram’s appearance from proof of cause.

mfg1-electrical-l054.title: Check the scope of ISO, JIS, and certification
mfg1-electrical-l054.objective: Distinguish what standards, certification, and individual inspections assess.

paragraphs.title: Products and management systems
paragraphs.text: ISO includes standards for products and methods as well as organizational management systems. ISO9001 concerns quality management, and ISO14001 environmental management. Organizational certification does not mean every product unconditionally passes.

paragraphs.title: Scope and edition
paragraphs.text: JIS means Japanese Industrial Standards. Basic, method, and product standards concern different targets. Check edition, scope, contract, and drawing requirements as well as the number. International alignment does not guarantee every requirement is identical.

paragraphs.title: Marks and instrument condition
paragraphs.text: A JIS mark concerns conformity of the specified product. A marked instrument’s reliability can still change through falls, wear, dirt, or calibration status. Do not substitute the mark for pre-use checks or the product’s inspection result.

terms.meaning: A system for verifying that its target meets defined requirements.
The range of things covered by a standard or document.
Establishing the relationship between an instrument’s indication and a reference.

terms.reading: にほんさんぎょうきかく
terms.meaning: The Japanese name of JIS.

mfg1-electrical-l054.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Separate ISO9001 certification, a product’s JIS marking, instrument calibration, and product acceptance into four categories. Explain what each can verify.
safety: Do not continue using damaged tools merely because they have certification or a mark.
mfg1-electrical-l054.summary: Distinguish what standards, certification, and individual inspections assess.

mfg1-electrical-l055.title: Connect SI base units and prefixes to calculations
mfg1-electrical-l055.objective: Separate base quantities from prefixes, and convert areas and time correctly.

paragraphs.title: Seven base units
paragraphs.text: The SI base units are length m, mass kg, time s, electric current A, thermodynamic temperature K, amount of substance mol, and luminous intensity cd. Voltage V, resistance Ω, and power W are derived units. Do not confuse mass kg with force N, or temperature K with Celsius.

paragraphs.title: Align prefixes
paragraphs.text: k means 1000 time s, m one thousandth, and μ one millionth.2.4 kΩ=2400 Ω,750 mA=0.750 A, and 2200 μF=2.2 mF. Lowercase m and uppercase M are different prefixes; preserve case.

paragraphs.title: Convert area and time
paragraphs.text: 1 mm²=10⁻⁶m²: the length conversion factor cannot be applied unchanged to area.30 minutes is 0.5 hours;1.2 kW for 30 minutes uses 0.6 kWh. Align units before substitution and attach a unit to the result.

terms.meaning: The International System of Units.
A symbol expressing a multiple or fraction of a unit.
A unit formed by combining base units.
A quantity expressing the extent of a surface.

mfg1-electrical-l055.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Convert 0.8 kΩ,25 mA,1500 μF, and 2 mm² to units without the prefixes. Calculate energy inWh for 900 W used for 20 minutes.
safety: Do not enter guessed settings with unknown units into real equipment.
mfg1-electrical-l055.summary: Separate base quantities from prefixes, and convert areas and time correctly.

mfg1-electrical-l056.title: Do not confuse pH, oxidation-reduction, and specific gravity
mfg1-electrical-l056.objective: Explain chemical indicators, reactions, and density ratios separately.

paragraphs.title: Acidity and alkalinity
paragraphs.text: pH is a dimensionless indicator of acidity or alkalinity in aqueous solution. In ordinary dilute-solution examples around 25°C, near 7 is neutral. This does not mean every liquid must have a pH from 0 to 14 or that neutral pH is 7 at every temperature.

paragraphs.title: Think in terms of electrons
paragraphs.text: Oxidation can be described as losing electrons, and reduction as gaining electrons. Combining with oxygen or losing oxygen are representative reaction examples. Oxidation and reduction occur together; do not judge process progress by color alone.

paragraphs.title: Compare equal volumes
paragraphs.text: For solids and liquids, specific gravity is a ratio to the density of reference water and has no unit. Density, expressed inkg/m³or similar units, is different. At specific gravity 2.5, equal volumes have 2.5 times the reference water’s mass; differing volumes change the mass comparison.

terms.meaning: An indicator of acidity or alkalinity in aqueous solution.
A change in which a substance loses electrons.
A change in which a substance gains electrons.
The ratio of a density to that of a reference substance.

mfg1-electrical-l056.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Find the mass of material with specific gravity 2.7 at the same volume as 40 g of reference water. Explain why pH is not equivalent to chemical hazard, and describe electron transfer in oxidation and reduction.
safety: Do not judge a chemical solution safe from pH or specific gravity alone; check its SDS.
mfg1-electrical-l056.summary: Explain chemical indicators, reactions, and density ratios separately.
